title: Reuse and cleanup
current: Lane lookup uses the public item reference and recorded branches; cleanup acts on a recorded branch, or on detached@<commit> when the checkout has no branch. A done item's lanes retire on the machine that holds them once each proves clean and landed; a preserved lane is named with its reason. One malformed lane in a prune batch is reported and skipped; the other lanes in that batch are still judged. A clean detached lane whose commit is on the target retires; a dirty or unmerged detached lane stays, with the reason named. A cancelled item's lanes are deleted outright — worktree (even dirty, locked or unmerged), local branch and origin branch — by the cancel on its own machine and by the next merged-lane sweep on every other machine, and each deletion's head SHAs land in the item's Progress Log under `Cancelled lanes deleted`. A standalone landing retires the item's own lanes and then runs the machine-wide merged-lane sweep. A deployment run's member close-out retires only that member's lanes; after every member has closed, the run runs that sweep once per distinct checkout. Run close-out prints each preserved lane as a `Lane cleanup warning:` with the doctor repair. `max_active_worktrees` counts lanes doing work: an item lane whose committed work already landed on its base holds no slot until release close-out retires it, while a lane that has not committed yet counts, and `HC-worktree-health` lists the landed lanes of open items on their own line. A hosted control plane settles runs where no lane lives, so lane creation at the cap runs the same sweep first and then refuses only for what remains, naming unmerged lanes to merge, finished deploy-run driver trees for `yoke watch doctor -- --only HC-worktree-health --fix`, an open run's driver tree as in use, and how many landed lanes it left out. A lane is disposable when git reports only named caches (including `.hypothesis`) or paths the project declares in `disposable_generated_paths`; any other ignored file preserves it.
